title: A protocol for isolation of target proteins of natural compounds
protocol: Incubate Magnetic FG beads with 10 mM 1-hydroxybenzotriazole, 10 mM 1-ethyl-3-(3-demethyaminopropyl)-carbodiimide HCl, and various concentrations of **1** in N,N-dimethylformamide for 4 hours at room temperature.
Mask unreacted residues using 20% carbonic anhydride in N,N-dimethylformamide.
Store beads at 4 °C.
Extract PC-3 cell fractions using ProteoExtract subcellular proteome extraction kit \(S-PEK).
Equilibrate Compound 1-immobilized beads and FG beads with 0.5% NP-40 lysis buffer.
Incubate cell protein fractions with beads for 4 hours at 4 °C.
Wash Beads five times with 100 mM KCl.
Wash beads with 1M KCl.
Perform SDS-PAGE on a 10% gel.
Stain the gel with silver staining.
Cut and treat the cutting gel with trypsin.
Analyze recovered peptides with electrospray ion trap mass spectrometer coupled online with nano-scale HPLC on a C18 column to acquire MS/MS spectra.
Use peptide mass fingerprinting for protein identification from tryptic fragment sizes using the Mascot search engine querying to the entire NCBI database of theoretical human peptide masses.
Use paclitaxel and vinblastine sulfate salt as stabilizing and destabilizing controls.
Fix tubulin on one electrode (ch1) for the assay.
Block another electrode absolutely with BSA (ch2) for reference.
Investigate compound affinity with tubulin using NAPiCOS QCM system.
Stabilize baseline with PBS/50% EtOH, flow rate set to 20 μl/min.
Inject one hundred microliters of each compound into the system to react with fixed tubulin to obtain differential frequency shift between ch1 and ch2.
Calculate Kd values by standard Scatchard analysis using frequency changes from several concentrations of compound.
Use Tubulin Polymerization Assay Kit to test tubulin polymerization on each compound.
Paclitaxel (Wako Co., Japan) and vinblastine were used as positive and negative controls, respectively.
Measure fluorescence using FlexStation3 (Molecular Devices, USA).
